items.prompt: A single COMAC C919 narrow-body twin-engine jet airliner, completely unpainted: pure clean white fuselage, wings and tail, with absolutely no livery, no logos, no airline titles, no registration and no cheatline. Exact aircraft identity, follow every point: overall length 38.9 metres and wingspan 35.8 metres, constant-diameter cylindrical fuselage 3.95 metres across, total height 11.95 metres — proportioned between an A320 and an A321, slightly longer and slenderer than an A320. Rounded, gently curved nose profile, smoother and more bulbous than an Airbus A320's nose. Cockpit glazing has EXACTLY FOUR windows total (not six): two large upright forward windshield panes with a DOWNSLOPING top edge (no notch, unlike Airbus), and two side windows whose lower edge comes to a distinct V-shaped point. Small dorsal fin blending the cockpit roofline into the fuselage. Fuselage windows are subtly RECTANGULAR with rounded corners, not oval. Two full passenger doors on each side plus two small overwing emergency exit hatches per side. Low-mounted wings swept back, wingtips curve sharply upward into a bent, curved winglet (not a straight blade sharklet). Two large-diameter CFM LEAP-1C turbofans slung on pylons under and forward of the wing leading edge; each nacelle inlet is a perfect circle, large fan face visible, polished inlet lip, visible exhaust cone. Conventional swept vertical fin, low-set horizontal stabilisers on the rear fuselage. Landing gear extended: twin-wheel nose gear, twin-wheel main gear under the wing roots.

A single COMAC ARJ21-700 regional jet airliner, completely unpainted: pure clean white fuselage, wings and tail, with absolutely no livery, no logos, no airline titles, no registration and no cheatline. Exact aircraft identity, follow every point: overall length 33.46 metres, wingspan 27.28 metres, fuselage diameter 3.2 metres, total height 8.44 metres. The fuselage cross-section and nose profile closely resemble a McDonnell Douglas MD-80 or DC-9: a narrow, slightly pointed nose and a slender tube fuselage, not an Airbus/Boeing-style rounded nose. Low-mounted, moderately swept wings positioned at mid-fuselage height, with small upturned winglets at each tip. A T-TAIL: the horizontal stabiliser is mounted at the very top of the vertical fin, well above the fuselage, not at the base. TWO ENGINES MOUNTED ON THE REAR FUSELAGE on short pylons on either side, just ahead of the tail, well behind and below the wings — the wings themselves carry NO engines. Each rear engine nacelle has a circular intake. Two passenger doors per side, small round cabin windows in a five-abreast single-aisle cabin. Long, tapering tailcone behind the rear-mounted engines, swept vertical fin rising to the T-tail. Landing gear extended: twin-wheel nose gear, twin-wheel main gear retracting into fuselage-side fairings (not wing-mounted, since the wing carries no engine pylons to hide gear near).

A single Antonov An-148 regional jet airliner, completely unpainted: pure clean white fuselage, wings and tail, with absolutely no livery, no logos, no airline titles, no registration and no cheatline. Exact aircraft identity, follow every point: overall length 29.13 metres, wingspan 28.91 metres, fuselage diameter 3.15 metres, total height 8.19 metres — a short, stubby regional jet, wingspan close to the fuselage length. High-mounted wings sitting ON TOP of the fuselage (high-wing configuration), swept back moderately, no winglets, plain rounded wingtips. A T-TAIL: horizontal stabiliser mounted at the very top of the swept vertical fin. Two Progress D-436-148 turbofans slung UNDER the high wings on short pylons, each nacelle a plain circular intake with a modest fan diameter, hanging well clear of the ground given the high-wing layout. Two passenger doors per side, small round cabin windows in a five-abreast single-aisle cabin, blunt rounded nose with a straightforward two-pilot cockpit glazing. Landing gear extended: twin-wheel nose gear tucked under the cockpit, twin-wheel main gear retracting into fuselage-side fairings low on the belly (the high wing carries no main gear).

A single Airbus A350-900ULR wide-body twin-engine jet airliner, completely unpainted: pure clean white fuselage, wings and tail, with absolutely no livery, no logos, no airline titles, no registration and no cheatline. Exact aircraft identity, follow every point: overall length 66.8 metres, wingspan 64.75 metres, fuselage diameter 5.96 metres, total height 17.05 metres. Distinctive Airbus A350 nose: a long, gently downward-drooped radome with a smoothly rounded profile, larger cockpit windows than the A330/A320 family. Low-mounted wings with a pronounced upward curve near the tip blending into a tall, gracefully curved BLENDED WINGLET (not a sharp sharklet blade). Two very large-diameter Rolls-Royce Trent XWB turbofans slung well forward and below the wing leading edge on short pylons; each nacelle has a distinctive scalloped, serrated (chevron-style) trailing edge on the exhaust cowl, a signature Trent XWB feature, with a large circular fan face and dark spinner. Two passenger doors per side plus two smaller doors further aft (four door pairs total, wide-body double-aisle cabin), oval cabin windows. Swept vertical fin with a curved leading edge, low-set swept horizontal stabilisers on the rear fuselage, small APU exhaust at the tailcone tip. Landing gear extended: twin-wheel nose gear, four-wheel bogie main gear retracting into the wing-body fairing.
